column2: Then drag out of the storeroom everything even slightly green!
I have a green hat. For sale. Cheap. Barely worn, only on jobs.
Beep-Beep From the Sky
That evening a tiny shiny star rolled over the rooftops. It went “beep-beep” and hid behind a cloud.
Is that a new doorbell? I didn't order one.
Unknown object in the sky. Security notes: it blinks in rhythm. Suspicious. But pretty.
Looks like someone far away said hello to us first.
(tick... tick...) I've heard that signal in the future. It's louder there.
The Dance Marathon
Tonight's a marathon: whoever dances longest gets a free milkshake. For life! I can't back out now.
I've been dancing for four hours. My feet hum. But at last the floor shines from my steps.
I pretended to faint and ate popcorn. Don't tell anyone.
I counted the spins. The winner is Capy. By a wide margin.
I just spin when I'm nervous. Thank you.
The Stormy Night
A storm hit so hard that every sign in the block went dark. The diner sank into darkness.
Without power the jukebox is silent. And without it I don't know where to look.
Let's light candles. It'll be warmer. And a little romantic.
I'll set out the candles. On two tables. The rest... they need to go somewhere too, right?
Notice: in the dark you can hear me better. Tick. Tock. Tick.
The Watch in the Jukebox
When the lights came back, the jukebox screen showed not a song title but “TICK”.
That was a lovely era, Capy. I liked the shakes, the milkshakes and those biplanes.
We're not done. Pip still needs help with the tables.
Help him. I'll wait. A minute more or less. I'm the Watch, after all.
Pip put on a new record. It was about a road that goes further than you can imagine.
The Ball That Fell
The town bloomed with candy-coloured lights. On the corner someone rehearses a tune you won't get out of your head.
I'm Zina. The wind tore down my mirror ball and it shattered. The party is tonight and I have no sparkle. At all.
We'll gather every piece. No sparkle, no party.
I estimate collecting the shards at four coins and one scratch. Mine.
Just don't leave the shards unattended. Especially with the raccoon around.
A Stripy Misunderstanding
Zina stepped outside and everyone went quiet: her stripes had turned rainbow, as if a rainbow had decided to be a zebra.
I only asked for a little colour! Who painted me?
Me. A free bonus with the “Sparkle” package. Thanks for trusting me.
Shnyr, you recoloured a whole zebra?
Not the whole thing. Only where I could reach.
A Mosaic of a Thousand Pieces
The new ball is made of a thousand tiny mirrors. They get glued on one by one. Stock up on patience. Or coffee.
I counted: eight hundred mirrors needed. Another two hundred I wrote down as spare. That's not greed, that's a plan.
What if I glue one upside down? Sparkle still sparkles.
Then the ball will play a bit in reverse. Suits us, honestly.
By morning the ball looked like a big star that had come down for a rest.
The Dance Floor Comes Alive
The sidewalk tiles light up in turn: pink, blue, yellow. Someone stepped, and the whole pavement hummed with bass.
That's my dance floor. It has a life of its own and it loves being danced on.
Warning: offenders of rhythm will be fined. In music. Slow music.
I invented the “quietly along the edge” technique. No fines, no adventures.
Everyone to the floor! Who can't dance will learn in three beats.
The Flares Contest
Today's contest: whose trousers are wider. The jury: me, Tonya and the accountant. Seriously.
I have no trousers. Is that a disqualification or a privilege?
That's an observation. By the way, the raccoon's trousers are a size bigger than needed.
Two spare pockets. They're not trousers, they're a warehouse. Toma would be jealous.
Everyone won. The widest trousers went to the clothes rack. It was just standing nearby.
The Silent Disco
That evening the block lost power. The music vanished with it.
Without speakers I'm helpless... no, wait. We have flashlights. We can sway them.
Then let's dance without music. Everyone listens to their own beat inside.
Inside me there's a march playing right now. Is that allowed?
In the dark hundreds of little lights moved and nobody stepped on anyone's foot. The wonder of the day.
The Last Song of the Night
The last song has to be special. I want Capy to choose it.
I don't know any... except the one the watch in my pocket hums.
(tick-tock, tick-tock-tock) Boom-boom, boom-ba-dum.
That's a real disco beat! Watch, you've got talent!
The whole block danced to the ticking until dawn. Someone even recorded it on tape.
Dawn Over the Dance Floor
At dawn the mirror ball caught the first ray and scattered a thousand bright spots across the walls.
That was the best party of my life. Thank you, Capy. Now I have a ball. And friends.
Congratulations. Disco is coming to an end, like any good tune.
And what comes next?
Next comes a world that lives in tiny pixels. Pack up when you can.
Insert Coin
The world became square, loud and a little flashy. Above the door a sign glows: INSERT COIN.
I'm Max. I run the best arcade in town. It wants a coin to start, and all I have left is faith.
Here's a coin. But the first turn is mine.
Wow, it worked the first time! Is that talent or just luck?
The screen flashed: “PLAYER 1: CAPY”. The first level began counting down.
A Record That Never Happened
On the high-score board a new name shines: “RAC — 999999”. Everyone slowly turned their heads.
I've beaten this game a hundred times and never saw that many points. Where from?
I'm just very diligent. And a bit handy with screwdrivers.
That score is larger than all the coins in town. Mathematically unfair.
Shnyr, screw it back and we'll forget about the record. Deal?
The Level With Ghosts
A maze appeared on the screen, and balloon-like blobs with eyes floated between the machines. They giggled.
Those are the ghosts from level one! They climbed out of the game and I never called them.
They're easier to catch when they turn blue. I know from experience. A long time ago.
To the machines! Whoever eats the most dots frees the hall!
I'll eat anything that isn't nailed down. Are dots tasty?
Falling Blocks
Colourful shapes slowly descend from the sky while lines swallow them row by row.
That's Tetris! We fit them into neat rows or they'll bury the whole street.
Straight ones left, crooked ones right. I've colour-coded it all. I actually like it.
Team, rotate the blocks! Whoever stands idle becomes a stick!
Rows vanished one by one and the street suddenly looked brighter, as if just cleaned.
The Secret Code
I know a secret: up-up-down-down-left-right... and B three times. It gives infinite lives.
Cheating. Honestly, such lives would cost eighty coins.
Mine's better: “up, right, right again and behind the till”. Someone always forgets their change there.
No codes. We play for real.
Max sighed but smiled for the first time that night. An honest game beats any hint.
The Level Boss
At the end of a long corridor stood a huge pixelated monster with a sign: “TAX OFFICE”.
Oh. An old acquaintance. Let me talk to it in the language of numbers.
We're with you, Spike. Each of us will throw a coin and an idea at it.
I'll distract it. I'll ask if it's expecting a gift.
The boss froze, blinked and broke into two hundred squares labelled “20% OFF”.
Game Over?
Suddenly every screen in the hall flickered and went dark. Only one line remained: GAME OVER.
No... That's it? Is this the end of my arcade?
No, Max. Look below, in small print: “CONTINUE? 10... 9... 8...”
We press Yes! All together! Three, two, one!
The screens lit up again, brighter than before. Max hugged Capy so hard a button creaked.
Continue?
When the guests left, one message remained on the main machine. It blinked to the rhythm of ticking.
“CONTINUE?” That's me asking, Capy. There are plenty of levels ahead.
Are you sure you're not a level boss?
